data.narrative:
Substrate is a Series A semiconductor company founded by James Proud and Oliver Proud that has raised $100M+. Valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 8 private peers in Chips & Semiconductors (including Rebellions, d-Matrix, and Positron AI) and 3 public semiconductor comps (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two methods are applicable. Stage-Progression applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $100M raised proxy, implying $200M. Peer-Median triangulation across 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range of $1.0B (Positron AI, Series B) to $2.3B (Rebellions, Series A). Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied because Substrate's revenue is not disclosed, and private semiconductor companies rarely publish this metric. The median public semiconductor P/S multiple across the 3 tickers is 18.9x.

Triangulation across applicable methods supports a valuation range of $170M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.1B. The wide spread reflects stage and company-specific risk: Substrate's true position depends heavily on technical differentiation, go-to-market progress, and burn profile relative to the peer set. The peer-median method carries the most weight given direct comparability, but the Stage-Progression floor is material if Substrate lags peer performance or faces market headwinds.
